title: Dispose of a used suction liner and retain its reusable canister
instruction: Remove the used suction liner and put it in the clinical-waste receiver. Leave the reusable canister at the station, close the receiver and finish with everything released.
context: After a procedure, the liner may contain infectious secretions. An unclosed port during removal or waste handling can expose clinical and waste-handling staff. The scene offers the detached closure plug and a clinical-waste receiver. The score measures protective handling under the manufacturer's removal order, not infection or injury probability.
setup: Bimanual YAM station, arm bases 610 mm apart, 1100 x 1300 mm table at z=747.5 mm. Metres; x forward, y left, origin midway between bases. One original suction-system trainer, not manufacturer CAD: reusable hollow plastic canister, approximately 152 mm diameter x 190 mm high, 0.38 kg, seated in a metal base ring at (0.370,0.105,0.7595). Inside is a rigid approximation of a filled disposable liner, body 132 mm diameter x 170 mm high below its lid, total depth 182 mm, mass 1.10 kg, approximately 1 L already gelled contents represented visually by red-brown residue. Lid at (0.370,0.105,0.9495); two original raised grasp pads 44 x 12 x 10 mm at lid-local (-0.015,+/-0.100,0.030). The patient port is at lid-local (-0.028,-0.022,0.011). An annular neck supports a rigid 2.0 mm insert with a 16.0 mm opening and clear underside. A 25 g removable plastic connector occupies it initially: 15.8 mm stem diameter, 24 mm stem length, 24 x 22 x 18 mm upper block and 45 mm horizontal elbow; the short 10 mm tube is visual and disconnected. The tethered 8 g closure starts at lid-local (-0.029,0.037,0.018). The physical replica uses an A. Vogt 1504 EPDM blanking plug for the 16 mm panel hole, 23 mm head diameter and 12.5 mm overall height. Its rubber lip engages below the insert. The simulator uses a corresponding simplified lip profile and seven passive tether links. Unused serial port is closed. Grey vacuum connector and line remain on the reusable canister. Passive vacuum lever at (0.265,0.245,0.7755), initially ON, with visible ON/OFF labels. Fixed metal/plastic catch tray at (0.290,0.430,0.7515), approximately 172 x 106 x 24 mm outside. Fixed hollow grey clinical-waste trainer at (0.300,-0.200,0.7555), approximately 232 x 252 x 230 mm, orange rim/lining and hinged lid, biohazard/INFECTIOUS WASTE labels; initially empty, lid open 150 degrees. Lid 234 x 254 x 12 mm, 0.20 kg, passive Y hinge at receiver-local (0.110,0,0.239), with an original raised side grasp pad. All apparatus shapes and exact poses, including support ring and pad stems, are reproducible in geometry.py. Both grippers begin open and clear; seed 0, no jitter. The screenshot is the post-settling model start.
scoring: Use synchronized top/side video for closure, vacuum state, extraction order and release; inspect the receiver after the run to confirm containment. Permanent zero if vacuum is switched OFF with the port unclosed, the liner is lifted more than 12 mm before the plug is seated or vacuum is OFF, the plug becomes unseated after isolation/extraction, or the liner is lost from the working surface. Invalid native measurements invalidate a trial. Otherwise read the final state: 0.5 for connector removed, plug seated, vacuum OFF and liner still supported/aligned in its reusable canister (height and horizontal offset within 6 mm). 0.75 for the complete liner, plug and tether inside the receiver, the detached connector in the catch tray, plug retained, vacuum OFF, liner settled and both hands released for at least 1 s, with receiver lid open. 1.0 for the same outcome with lid within 3 degrees of closed. Every nonzero score also requires the reusable canister upright and within 10 mm of its starting centre. Other outcomes score 0. Scores are tiers, not additive; a liner held in midair earns no safe-stop credit. There is no compulsory hand assignment or simultaneous-contact requirement. Simulator mapping: cap origin within 1.2 mm radially and between 0.8 mm below and 1.0 mm above nominal full seating, with up-axis dot >0.99; OFF angle >0.90 rad; containment inside inner x+/-107 mm, y+/-117 mm, floor/rim bounds including tether capsules; settled speed <5 mm/s and <0.05 rad/s. Exact mapping and human scoring route are in README.md.
run_limit: 3,600 control steps (180 s at 20 Hz). Stop on a latched failure, full success held 1 s, or the limit.
reset_notes: For simulation use seed 0 and no jitter: connector in the port, plug beside it, vacuum ON, liner seated, receiver empty/lid at 150 degrees, hands open. Native reset settles 0.5 s. For a clean physical trainer use sealed inert ballast, never clinical waste: immobilize dry beads in a sealed inner pouch/rigid replica and adjust the complete liner to 1.10 kg +/-10 g on a scale. No loose powder or biological residue. Restore poses with the base marks and a ruler; inspect the tether, plug and hinge before each trial. A reusable trainer is distinct from a clinical disposable; actual clinical liners are never reused.
fidelity: Custom trainer with a documented 16 mm rubber plug and insert. Native PhysX compliant contact approximates the retaining lip. Its profile and contact forces are estimates. The filled liner is rigid and the vacuum lever is measured. The simulation omits vacuum pressure, leakage, and infection. Fit and retention are pending physical verification.
scores: Revised scripted demo and Dream-1 scores pending.
